title: Inner Tank Boost Pump — Installation
abstract: Installation of one inner tank boost pump with a new flange seal, followed by tank closure, refuelling and a leak check at operating pressure with the dry bay drains under observation.

sections.purpose: This task gives the installation of one inner tank boost pump, the closure of the tank and the leak and functional checks that must be complete before the aircraft is released.
sections.job_setup_note: Confirm the inlet housing standard fitted at the position, because the restrictor mounting differs between the two and the harness clipping changes with it. The flange seal is always new. Plan the sealant cure time into the schedule; the tank cannot be refuelled until the cure is complete, and that drives the elapsed time more than the installation itself.
sections.procedure: Confirm that the atmosphere in the tank is still safe and that the entry watch is posted. Count the tools and the loose items into the tank. Clean the flange land and inspect it for damage. Fit the new flange seal, using anchor nuts EN968165-23 and swaged collars LN41340-8C at the joint. CAUTION: DO NOT RE-USE A FLANGE SEAL, EVEN IF IT LOOKS UNDAMAGED. A COMPRESSED SEAL WILL PASS THE LEAK CHECK COLD AND WEEP IN SERVICE. Offer the pump into the aperture and engage it squarely. Install the retaining fasteners and torque them in the sequence and to the values of the illustration. Install the restrictor NY844698-29 at the position for the housing standard fitted and re-clip the harness of the sensor NYD659955-61 clear of it. Connect the pump connector and do a continuity and insulation check; enter the result in the job card. Apply the tank sealant at the joint and record the cure start time. Count the tools and the loose items out and confirm the count. Refit the wing tank access panel with a new seal. WARNING: DO NOT REFUEL BEFORE THE SEALANT CURE TIME HAS PASSED. A JOINT THAT IS PRESSURISED DURING CURE WILL LEAK AND THE TANK WILL HAVE TO BE OPENED AGAIN.
sections.close_out: Refuel the tank after the cure time and do a leak check at operating pressure with the dry bay drains under observation for thirty minutes. Run the pump and record the delivery pressure and the current. Record the tool count, the sealant batch and cure times, and the leak check result. Close the technical log entry made at removal.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Use the outboard restrictor position and the revised harness clipping on aircraft at the replacement inlet housing standard.

safety_precautions: Keep the entry watch posted while anybody is inside the tank.
Do not refuel before the sealant cure time has passed.
Count every tool and loose item into and out of the tank.

title: Inner Tank Boost Pump — Installation

issue.reason: Bonding resistance at the flange joint is now a measured value released against the aircraft, with the acceptance limit stated in the task rather than left to the job card.

abstract: Installation of one inner tank boost pump with a new flange seal, the bonding resistance measurement released against the aircraft, and tank closure, refuelling and a leak check at operating pressure with the dry bay drains under observation.

sections.purpose: This task gives the installation of one inner tank boost pump, the closure of the tank and the leak and functional checks that must be complete before the aircraft is released.
sections.job_setup_note: Confirm the inlet housing standard fitted at the position, because the restrictor mounting differs between the two and the harness clipping changes with it. The flange seal is always new. The bonding resistance at the flange joint is part of the structural lightning protection argument for the dry bay, so it is a released measurement and not a workshop reading: take the bonding tester into the tank with the rest of the equipment and count it in and out. Plan the sealant cure time into the schedule; the tank cannot be refuelled until the cure is complete, and that drives the elapsed time more than the installation itself.
sections.procedure: Confirm that the atmosphere in the tank is still safe and that the entry watch is posted. Count the tools and the loose items into the tank. Clean the flange land and inspect it for damage. Fit the new flange seal, using anchor nuts EN968165-23 and swaged collars LN41340-8C at the joint. CAUTION: DO NOT RE-USE A FLANGE SEAL, EVEN IF IT LOOKS UNDAMAGED. A COMPRESSED SEAL WILL PASS THE LEAK CHECK COLD AND WEEP IN SERVICE. Offer the pump into the aperture and engage it squarely. Install the retaining fasteners and torque them in the sequence and to the values of the illustration. Measure the bonding resistance between the pump body and the tank structure at the two points shown in the illustration, before any sealant is applied, and confirm that each reading is not more than 2.5 milliohms. CAUTION: DO NOT ACCEPT A BONDING READING TAKEN AFTER THE SEALANT HAS BEEN APPLIED. THE MEASUREMENT IS PART OF THE DRY BAY LIGHTNING PROTECTION EVIDENCE AND MUST BE REPEATABLE. Install the restrictor NY844698-29 at the position for the housing standard fitted and re-clip the harness of the sensor NYD659955-61 clear of it. Connect the pump connector and do a continuity and insulation check. Apply the tank sealant at the joint and record the cure start time. Count the tools and the loose items out and confirm the count. Refit the wing tank access panel with a new seal. WARNING: DO NOT REFUEL BEFORE THE SEALANT CURE TIME HAS PASSED. A JOINT THAT IS PRESSURISED DURING CURE WILL LEAK AND THE TANK WILL HAVE TO BE OPENED AGAIN.
sections.close_out: Refuel the tank after the cure time and do a leak check at operating pressure with the dry bay drains under observation for thirty minutes. Run the pump and record the delivery pressure and the current. Release the two bonding resistance values against the aircraft registration and the pump position; a job card entry alone does not close this task, because the values have to be retrievable at the next dry bay assessment. Record the tool count, the sealant batch and cure times, and the leak check result. Close the technical log entry made at removal.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Use the outboard restrictor position and the revised harness clipping on aircraft at the replacement inlet housing standard. The bonding resistance values are released against the aircraft at every position, at both housing standards.

safety_precautions: Keep the entry watch posted while anybody is inside the tank.
Do not refuel before the sealant cure time has passed.
Count every tool and loose item into and out of the tank.
Take the bonding reading before any sealant is applied.
